passage: On the metro back from the seminar, Nikita turned it over in her head. The speaker had said the "special price" was for today only, and her classmate Hansa had already taken out a card. Nikita had felt the pull too: the warm room, the clapping, the ticking clock. "If I decide in that room, I'm deciding with everyone watching," she thought. "So I'll decide somewhere else." Back at her desk in the Delhi flat she wrote on a sticky note: No signature, no payment and no big life change on the same day as a meeting. Sleep on it. She stuck it to her laptop lid. "A rule is easier than willpower," she typed to Hansa. "Wait till tomorrow?" Hansa replied with a thumbs-up.

"They gave you a form?" Uday asked as Lokesh sat down in the hostel room.
"For a residential retreat. They said sign tonight and get the discount."
"And?"
"I didn't." Lokesh put the form on the desk. "I made a rule before I went. Never sign, never pay, never agree to move anywhere on the same day as a meeting. Always sleep on it."
"Why so strict?"
"Because in that room, with everyone smiling and the music, I'd say yes to anything. Tomorrow morning, alone, I'll actually read it."
"What if the discount's gone?"
"Then it's gone. If an offer only works when I can't think, it's not a good offer."
The next morning Lokesh read the form over tea. Page three said the retreat fee couldn't be refunded and that he'd live in the group house for the period. He tore it in half. "Glad I slept."

qa.q: What did page three of the form say?
qa.a: It said the retreat fee couldn't be refunded and he'd live in the group house for the period.

qa.q: Why did Lokesh make his rule, and what was he wary of?
qa.a: He was wary of his own feelings in the room, knowing that with smiles and music he'd feel pulled to say yes to anything.

qa.q: What else could Lokesh add to his rule?
qa.a: He could also show any form to a trusted person like Uday before deciding, adding a second check to sleeping on it.

qa.q: How might Uday see Lokesh's rule?
qa.a: Uday seems doubtful at first, but likely feels reassured seeing Lokesh tear the form after reading it.

grounding: Shows the student pre-committing to never sign, pay or move on the day of a meeting and to sleep on any request, guarding against pressure.

passage:
Before my third visit to the "success circle", I sat on my bed and made myself a promise. I'd noticed that at every meeting, someone ended the night signing up for something: a course, a monthly payment, a room in the group's flat. Always on the day. Always while everyone clapped.
I thought, if I decide the rule now, when I'm calm, I don't have to be strong later. So I wrote it in my notebook: I don't sign, pay or agree to move on the same day as a meeting. Every request waits one night.
At that meeting the leader asked me, in front of everyone, to join the "inner circle". It came with a fee. My friend Farida, who'd come with me, looked at me.
I said, "I'll let you know tomorrow." The room went quiet. The next morning, reading the terms alone, I said no. I'm Devika, and that rule was the easiest decision I ever made.

qa.q: Who came to the meeting with Devika?
How did Devika feel when asked to join in front of everyone?
qa.a: Devika likely felt pressured and exposed with the room watching, but steady because the rule was already decided.

qa.q: What else could Devika do after saying no?
qa.a: Devika could talk to Farida about stepping back from the circle altogether, since pressure in front of a crowd is a warning sign.

qa.q: How might Farida have felt watching Devika's answer?
qa.a: Farida was probably anxious when the leader asked and relieved and impressed when Devika calmly said 'tomorrow'.

grounding: Shows the student deciding in advance never to sign, pay or move on the day of a meeting and to sleep on every request, guarding against pressure.
